record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: Which generalized classes of semimeasures, Bayesian mixtures over those classes, and corresponding generalized randomness notions yield robust convergence results, and can structural conditions such as denseness characterize when such convergence holds and when it fails?

evidence.quote: j) Generalized mixtures and convergence concepts. Another interesting and potentially fruitful approach to the above convergence problem is to consider other classes of semimeasures M [Sch02b, Sch02a, Hut03b], define mixtures ξ over M, and (possibly) generalized randomness concepts by using this ξ to define a generalized notion of randomness. Using this approach, in [Hut06b] it has been shown that convergence holds for a subclass of Bernoulli distributions if the class is dense, but fails if the class is gappy, showing that a denseness characterization of M could be promising in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $\mathcal{X}=\{0,1\}$ and consider sequences in $\mathcal{X}^\infty$. A semimeasure on $\mathcal{X}^*$ is a function $\nu:\mathcal{X}^*\to[0,1]$ with $\nu(\epsilon)\le 1$ and $\nu(x)\ge \nu(x0)+\nu(x1)$ for all finite strings $x$; it is a (probability) measure when these inequalities are equalities. Given a countable class $\mathcal{M}$ of semimeasures together with a strictly positive prior weight $w:\mathcal{M}\to(0,1]$ with $\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal{M}} w(\nu)\le 1$, the Bayesian mixture is
$$\xi_{\mathcal{M}}(x)=\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal{M}} w(\nu)\,\nu(x).$$
For a true measure $\mu\in\mathcal{M}$, one studies posterior convergence of the predictive ratios $\xi_{\mathcal{M}}(x_{n+1}\mid x_{1:n})\to \mu(x_{n+1}\mid x_{1:n})$ along sequences $x_{1:\infty}$, where the convergence may be required $\mu$-almost surely, on every $\mu$-Martin-Löf random sequence, or on every sequence random with respect to a generalized randomness notion derived from $\xi_{\mathcal{M}}$ itself.

Known facts. Restrict to the class of Bernoulli measures $\mu_\theta$, $\theta\in\Theta\subseteq[0,1]$. It is known that if $\Theta$ is dense in $[0,1]$ then the mixture $\xi_\Theta$ predicts correctly on every $\mu_\theta$-random sequence for $\theta\in\Theta$, while if $\Theta$ has a gap (an open subinterval disjoint from $\Theta$) then convergence can fail on some random sequence.

Problem. Identify general classes $\mathcal{M}$ of semimeasures (extending beyond the computably enumerable universal class) such that:

(a) the corresponding Bayesian mixture $\xi_{\mathcal{M}}$ admits a well-defined generalized randomness notion (e.g. defined by Martin-Löf-type tests with respect to $\xi_{\mathcal{M}}$);

(b) for every $\mu\in\mathcal{M}$, the posterior $\xi_{\mathcal{M}}(\cdot\mid x_{1:n})$ converges to $\mu(\cdot\mid x_{1:n})$ on every sequence that is random in this generalized sense.

In particular, determine whether a topological/structural condition of "denseness" of $\mathcal{M}$ in an appropriate ambient space of semimeasures characterizes exactly when such robust convergence holds, and identify a structural property (analogous to the gappy/dense dichotomy for Bernoulli classes) whose violation provably forces convergence to fail on some random sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature (Hutter and collaborators, 2003–2007) establishes the dense-vs-gappy dichotomy for Bernoulli subclasses and constructs universal semimeasures that fail to converge on some Martin-Löf random sequences. A general characterization, in terms of denseness or another structural property, of which classes of semimeasures yield posterior convergence on all (generalized) random sequences does not appear to have been established; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Semimeasures Predicting Martin-Löf Random Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: There are universal semimeasures M which do not converge for all random sequences, i.e. a partial negative answer to the open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence on all Martin-Löf random sequences fails for some universal semimeasures, leaving the general characterization open.

status_evidence.title: Universal Convergence of Semimeasures on Individual Random Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence fails (holds) on generalized-random sequences in gappy (dense) Bernoulli classes.
status_evidence.claim: Denseness/gappiness gives a sharp dichotomy in the Bernoulli case, but a general structural characterization is not provided.

status_evidence.title: On Generalized Computable Universal Priors and their Convergence
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates a hierarchy of computability classes (finitely computable, estimable, enumerable, approximable) and convergence of associated mixtures.
status_evidence.claim: Different classes of semimeasures yield different convergence behavior; a general denseness-style characterization is not established.
